key_insight: Adaptive switching between cheap and expensive LLM oracles can minimize total cost while preserving downstream optimization accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For data curation and optimization pipelines, the paper gives a principled way to decide when higher-fidelity LLM calls are worth paying for.
method: Develops a restarted, cost-aware meta-algorithm that switches oracle fidelity when bias is known.
Introduces a budgeted certification scheme with occasional trusted-gradient checks when bias is unknown.
Implements the framework with biased stochastic gradient extrapolation and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise.
evidence_signal: Synthetic experiments and LLM-completion tests show the adaptive policy skips multiple expensive oracle calls, lowers cumulative cost, and matches the accuracy of fixed high-fidelity methods.
watch_item: The approach relies on occasional trusted evaluations and assumptions about bias/noise structure, so real-world gains depend on how well those conditions hold.
paper_title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
